Project: California State University Campuses Across the State  
Description: The map locates the geographical location of each California State University within the boundaries of California. The intentional orange halo around the border was to provide focus on the Universities. The map includes all the imperative cartography features such as the legend, north arrow, title, scale bar, and sources. The symbology of the map was meant to define the locations of the Cal States against the display of the local cities and intersections. For simplicity, the airlines were given appropriate symbology: black font airplane icons to indicate the locations of airports near California Universities. The highways are differentiated with light gray lines across the California counties, whereas California Counties are symbolized in black for distinction. This map was completed for Professor Jeremy Huey at Pasadena City College.

Project: The Mojave National Preserve Desert Solitude in Southern California  
Description: The Mojave National Preserve is located in Southern California, where it offers a diverse mosaic of ecological habitats and rich geologic history, with a variety of ranges in elevation throughout the park that make its landscapes rich. The preserve serves as the focal point for the map’s layout. Within the boundaries of the preserve, points of interest (major sites in the Mojave Desert) are pinpointed in red dots across the map. Towns are also depicted using yellow diamond-shaped stars, a symbology for simple viewing. Furthermore, the dark green-shaded regions are wilderness zones within the national preserve boundaries, which overlap with the light green shading of the preserve itself. Cartographic elements such as a north arrow, scale bar, legend, author name, and sources are included in the layout as illustrated above. The legend shows all of the labeled symbology icons surrounding the map, and the North arrow design is positioned on the far right for viewer visibility. This map was created for Professor Jeremy Huey at Pasadena City College.

Project: Population Census of the United 48 Lower States   
Description: For this project, we used population data from ArcGIS Online databases to show which countries had higher population density. We used multiple map layouts from the same database to represent the same information with different quantitative data, such as dot density, a graduated colors map, and a simple single symbol map. This map was completed for Professor Jeremy Huey at Pasadena City College.

The objective of this map is to identify and visualize energy conservation and zero-emission transportation features at the Disneyland Resort in Anaheim, California. The map focuses on the Disneyland Resort and surrounding Anaheim area to provide geographic context for the sustainability features. I created the map in ArcGIS Pro using point and line features to represent different energy-related initiatives. Point features were used to identify locations such as the Anaheim Green Power Program, solar installation, Autopia electrification, the Mark Twain Riverboat, Disneyland Railroad, Mickey & Friends Parking Structure, Pixar Pals Parking Structure, and Toy Story Parking Area. The Disneyland Railroad and Mark Twain Riverboat were included as biodiesel-powered attractions, while Autopia represents the resort's transition toward electric transportation. A green railroad line was used to represent Disneyland's zero-emission transportation system, allowing the transportation feature to be distinguished from the individual energy conservation locations. I used symbols (such as the sun symbol for energy) and labels to make each sustainability feature easy to locate and identify while keeping the map readable. An aerial-style basemap was selected to provide recognizable geographic features, streets, buildings, and surrounding areas without overpowering the sustainability symbols. The map also includes a legend, north arrow, scale bar, title, author name, and data source information as important cartographic elements. The scale bar provides distance information, while the north arrow helps the viewer understand direction. Labels identify major sustainability features and surrounding geographic locations to provide context. Overall, the cartographic design emphasizes the spatial distribution of Disneyland's energy conservation and zero-emission transportation initiatives while maintaining a clear and organized layout.

This map displays impaired and assessed water bodies throughout Orange County, California, using 2024 water-quality assessment data. The map uses qualitative categorical data represented with line and polygon features and produces a unique-values map. An impaired body of water is a river, stream, lake, or other surface water that does not meet established water-quality standards for one or more uses. Separate line and polygon layers were used to represent rivers, streams, and larger water bodies. Unique values distinguish between Listed and Not Listed features. Listed water bodies have one or more identified water-quality impairments under Section 303(d) of the Clean Water Act, while Not Listed water bodies do not have a 303(d) impairment listing in the 2024 assessment. I used darker blue symbols for Listed water bodies and lighter blue symbols for Not Listed water bodies so the difference could be identified quickly. Polygon features were made partially transparent so that geographic information underneath remained visible. A topographic basemap, city labels, Orange County boundary, State Plane projection, legend, north arrow, and scale bar were included to provide geographic context while keeping the map readable and balanced. 

This map displays population density by census tract throughout Orange County, California, using 2020 U.S. Census data. The map uses quantitative numerical data represented with polygon features and produces a graduated-color choropleth map. Population density is shown with graduated colors, where lighter shades indicate areas with lower population density and darker shades indicate areas with higher population density. The map shows that the more densely populated census tracts are generally concentrated in the northern and central portions of Orange County, including areas near Anaheim and Santa Ana, while many larger census tracts in eastern and southern Orange County have lower population densities. A five-class Natural Breaks (Jenks) classification was used to group census tracts into meaningful population-density ranges and make spatial differences easier to identify. The map also includes city labels, an Orange County boundary, a legend, a north arrow, scale information, and a light gray basemap for geographic context. Overall, the map demonstrates how population is unevenly distributed across Orange County and highlights the contrast between densely developed urban areas and less densely populated areas.
